dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Good afternoon, Kevin. Hello, and I hope you are having a good Monday. My name is Samir Okafor. Thank you for taking my call.
Sure, no problem. What can I do for you, Mr. Okafor?
Thank you, you are very kind. I am calling because of the storm last weekend, the nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday. There is some damage near my house, and I am not sure who I should speak to.
Okay. What kind of damage are we talking about?
A tree. Well, not the whole tree. A large limb has broken and it is hanging over the sidewalk. It is still attached a little, so it is hanging down, and people walk under it.
Gotcha. So a broken limb, hanging over the sidewalk, from the storm. Is it on the road at all, or just the sidewalk?

Only the sidewalk, I think. The end of it is close to the street, but it is not blocking the cars. I want to ask directly, please. Who do I call to report a downed tree? Is it you, the city, or is it the owner of the tree, or perhaps the electric company?

Good question, it depends a little. If it's a city tree, like on the street side of the sidewalk, that's us, the tree crew. If it's on private property, it's usually the owner who has to deal with it. And if it's tangled up in wires, that's the utility, and you'd want to stay well away from it. Are there any wires near it?
No, I do not see wires touching it. The wires are further down, I believe. It is only the limb.
Okay, good. What's the address?

Yes, it is 388 Dean Avenue. We are in the Fifth Ward, near Easton's Beach. Very close. The parking lot at the beach is empty now, so it is quiet, and nobody is there, but still some people walk on this sidewalk.
Yeah, this time of year it's pretty empty down there. Okay, 388 Dean Avenue. Now, is the tree in front of your house, or is it the neighbor's?
It is the tree next to the sidewalk, in front of my house. But I am honestly not sure if the tree belongs to me or to the city. I have not measured. I do not know how to tell.

That's fine, that's common. Usually if the trunk is between the sidewalk and the street, in that grass strip, it's a city tree. If the trunk is back on your side of the sidewalk, it's yours. Which is it, roughly?
Let me think. I am looking at it from the window now. The trunk is, I believe, between the sidewalk and the street. In the strip of grass, as you say.

Okay, then it's most likely a city tree. I'll put in a request for the tree crew to come take a look. They'll check ownership when they get out there. I'm writing down: limb broken, hanging over the sidewalk, 388 Dean Avenue, from the nor'easter.
Yes, exactly. Thank you very much. That is correct.
Can I get a number in case the crew needs to reach you?
Of course. It is 401-555-0179.
Got it, 401-555-0179. Now, they've got a lot of calls after the weekend, so I can't tell you the exact day they'll be out. But it's logged as a hazard over the sidewalk, so that helps.
I understand completely. Is there something I should do in the meantime? Should I put something there, a cone or a rope?
If you've got something to mark it off, that wouldn't hurt. Just don't try to pull it down yourself, especially if it's still hanging. Let the crew handle it.
Yes, I will not touch it. I will keep my family away. Thank you, Kevin, and may you have a good afternoon.
You too, Mr. Okafor. Take care.
